newsitem.title: USA: U.S. religious leaders demand environmental justice.
newsitem.headline: U.S. religious leaders demand environmental justice.

text.p: Twenty-five religious leaders from across the country Thursday launched a campaign for "environmental justice" for people in inner cities and poor rural areas who often bear the brunt of pollution and environmental degradation.

After meetings with Vice President Al Gore and Republican congressional leaders, the coalition National Religious Partnership for the Environment said it will launch a three-year $4 million campaign to push for policies that distribute environmental protections more fairly between suburbs and cities, and the rich and poor.

"At the front and centre of our shared religious concern is our fear of a broad bipartisan retreat from a commitment to the poor," Rev. William Skylstad, chairman of the U.S. Catholic Conference domestic policy commitee, said at a news conference.
Others in the coalition are the National Council of Churches of Christ, a federation of evangelical Christian agencies, eastern Orthodox communions and Jewish Life organisations.

The religious leaders said they were heartened that the Environmental Protection Agency was making special efforts to target regulations to protect children, but said it should not neglect the elderly, or the poor and minorities.

They also said they were encouraged that the EPA proposed stricter air quality standards, but were concerned that it proposed averaging air quality over broader areas so dirty urban air could be offset by cleaner suburban air.
